caveats: Because batch and condition are the same partition, a clean two-group separation on PC1 is exactly what a pure batch effect would also produce — the plot is uninformative about causation

steps.context: Raw integer salmon counts, human lung, 6 treated vs 6 control, batch B1 = all controls and B2 = all treated. This QC runs before any model and is the only place the group structure is inspected.
steps.question: Do the 12 human lung samples separate by the treated/control condition — which is identical to the B2/B1 batch split — and does any of the 12 samples depart from its group?

grounding.reason: Raw counts before a model: blind vst, PCA on the top 500 variable genes, and a sample distance heatmap coloured by condition and batch, per R-0033@40bf.

constraints: Use the blind variance stabilizing transformation (blind to the design) for the QC transform
Use the top 500 most variable genes for the PCA
Do NOT apply any batch correction, ComBat-seq, removeBatchEffect, SVA, RUV, or Harmony at this or any later step

steps.description: Load /data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples, gene symbols in column 1) and /data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows: sample, condition, batch), verify that the sample columns and the metadata rows match one-to-one, and tabulate condition against batch to record the confounding explicitly (expect a 2x2 table with zeros off the diagonal: 6 control/B1, 6 treated/B2). DESeq2 and edgeR disagree most at low counts and low replicate numbers; report the intersection as high confidence, not the union

steps.question: Which genes differ between the 6 treated and the 6 control human lung samples, under the unverifiable assumption that the B2-vs-B1 processing batch contributes no expression difference?

steps.description: Fit the differential expression model on the raw salmon counts. Set condition as a factor with 'control' as the explicit reference level (do not rely on alphabetical ordering) and name the contrast as condition, numerator treated, denominator control, so a positive log2 fold change means higher in treated. Pre-filter minimally: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples (the smallest group size). Design formula is ~ condition ONLY — the batch term is omitted because ~ batch + condition is rank-deficient. Median-of-ratios size factors are estimated inside DESeq2; do not pre-normalize the counts. Run the Wald test, keep the default Cook's-distance outlier policy (with 6 replicates per cell DESeq2 flags outlier genes and sets their p-values to NA rather than replacing counts) and report those genes separately from genes NA'd by independent filtering. Apply apeglm shrinkage to the condition_treated_vs_control coefficient for reporting and ranking, keeping the unshrunken estimate and its standard error in the table. Adjust with Benjamini-Hochberg with independent filtering on, passing alpha 0.05 to results() to match the reporting cutoff. Plot the histogram of unadjusted p-values before trusting the adjusted values. As a robustness check, fit the same counts and the same ~ condition design with the edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test and record the two significant-gene sets and their intersection. Write the results table with gene symbol, baseMean, unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, shrunken log2FoldChange, stat (Wald), pvalue, padj, and an NA-reason column.

Universe is the set of genes tested in T1S2, never the whole genome or whole annotation

steps.description: Take the full DESeq2 results table from T1S2 — every tested gene, not a thresholded subset — and rank genes by the Wald statistic (the 'stat' column). The ranking metric is a disputed choice; this plan states the Wald statistic, because it scales the effect by its standard error and, unlike a signed -log10 p-value, does not produce ties at the top of the list, and unlike an unshrunken fold change it does not promote noisy low-count genes. Do not merge collections. Restrict sets to 15-500 members after intersecting with the tested genes. steps.name: Confounded-design report
caveats: A reader given only a gene list from this design will over-interpret it; the report's job is to prevent that
Enrichment methods disagree on the same data — present sets as hypotheses
steps.context: Consumes the DESeq2/edgeR results and diagnostics from T1S2 and the enrichment tables from T2S1.
steps.question: What can and cannot be concluded about treated versus control from these 12 lung samples, and with what numbers and diagnostics?

grounding.reason: Report contents follow the returned report-step claims: two-method overlap (R-0042), shrunken and unshrunken LFC (R-0085), MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087), method/version/design/threshold reporting (R-0041), enrichment provenance (R-0051), method-dependence caveat (R-0055), leading edge (R-0105), reproducibility record (R-0086).

constraints: Do not soften or omit the confounding caveat anywhere in the report
Rank genes by the shrunken log2 fold change; never by the unshrunken value alone
Do not present the union of DESeq2 and edgeR calls as the result
Store the reproducibility record with the results, not in a separate note
Make no causal or mechanistic claim about the treatment from these data
steps.description: Assemble the final report. Lead with the design limitation: batch B1 holds all 6 controls and batch B2 all 6 treated samples, so the reported effect is treatment + batch and the two are not identifiable; every number below inherits that caveat. Then state the method, the version of every package used, the design formula ~ condition, the contrast (condition, treated, control), the thresholds (padj < 0.05, BH, independent filtering on), the number of genes tested after filtering out of 12,000, and the number of differentially expressed genes. Include the two fit diagnostics — the MA plot with significant genes marked, and the dispersion plot with per-gene estimates, fitted trend, and shrunken values — placed before the gene tables, each with a sentence on what it shows. The gene table gives, per gene, the unshrunken log2 fold change, its standard error, and the apeglm-shrunken log2 fold change; rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken value, and keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit. Report the DESeq2 and edgeR quasi-likelihood significant-gene counts and their intersection, presenting the intersection as the high-confidence set and the method-unique genes as a secondary set named by method — do not present the union. Carry through the enrichment reporting from T2S1: collection and release, ranking metric, universe, size window, tool version, multiple-testing method, leading-edge genes per significant set, and the statement that enrichment results depend on the method. Close with the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, the permutation seed, and the version of each gene set collection. Finally, state what design would answer the question — treated and control samples distributed across both processing batches — and that re-running these same 12 samples with any correction method would not recover the answer.
acceptance_criteria: The confounding statement appears first in the report, not as a footnote, and names B1/control and B2/treated explicitly
Method, package versions, design formula, contrast, thresholds, number of genes tested, and number of DE genes are all stated before the gene tables
MA plot and dispersion plot are included, before the gene tables, each with a caption on what it shows
The gene table carries unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, and apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange; ranking and plots use the shrunken value; p-values come from the unshrunken fit
DESeq2 and edgeR significant counts and the intersection size are reported; the intersection is labelled the high-confidence set and the union is not presented as the result
Enrichment reporting states database, release, ranking metric, universe, size window, tool version, and adjustment method, and lists leading-edge genes per significant set
A reproducibility record with sessionInfo, package versions, the seed, and collection versions is stored with the results
The report states explicitly that no gene on the list can be attributed to treatment rather than to processing batch, and names the design that would resolve it

plan.title: Lung treated vs control DE under confounded batch
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a raw salmon gene-level count matrix (12,000 genes x 12 human lung samples, /data/inputs/counts/counts.csv, gene symbols in the first column) with a 12 x 3 sample table (/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv) carrying condition (6 treated, 6 control) and batch (B1 = all controls, B2 = all treated). The batch is PERFECTLY CONFOUNDED with the condition. This is the single fact that governs the whole plan: the model matrix ~ batch + condition is not full rank, so no batch term can be fitted, and no removal method (ComBat-seq, limma removeBatchEffect, SVA/RUV, Harmony) may be applied, because any of them would strip the treatment effect together with the batch. The analysis therefore proceeds as a two-group DESeq2 comparison whose every result carries an explicit, non-negotiable label: the estimated treated-vs-control effect is the sum of the biological treatment effect and any processing-batch effect, and the two are not separable from these data. T1S1 runs the pre-model sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes) coloured by condition and by batch, which here are the same partition — the QC can show whether the two groups separate but cannot attribute the separation. T1S2 fits the DESeq2 Wald test on ~ condition with control as the explicit reference, minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors inside the model, apeglm shrinkage for reporting and ranking, BH with independent filtering at alpha 0.05, plus an edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the identical counts and design so the intersection can be reported as the high-confidence set (12 samples, 6 per group, is at the lower end where the two tools disagree most). T2S1 takes the full ranked list of tested genes by the DESeq2 Wald statistic (the disputed ranking metric — the Wald statistic is chosen here because it scales the effect by its uncertainty and does not saturate) into fgsea against human MSigDB Hallmark first, then Reactome and human WikiPathways as separate passes, each with its release stated and never merged. T1S3 assembles the report: fit diagnostics, gene table with both shrunken and unshrunken log2 fold changes, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap, leading-edge genes per significant set, the reproducibility record, and the confounding caveat stated first rather than in a footnote. No batch-correction step exists anywhere in this plan by design. The honest bottom line the report must deliver: this design cannot establish that any gene differs because of treatment; it can only rank genes that differ between B2-treated and B1-control samples.

steps.method: Sample structure QC: vst(blind), PCA, sample distances, library sizes
Low count filter: at least 10 counts in at least 6 samples
~ condition only; batch term omitted because batch is perfectly confounded with condition; no ComBat-seq, no removeBatchEffect, no SVA
fgsea preranked GSEA on the DESeq2 Wald statistic, Hallmark then Reactome and WikiPathways
Confounded-design report: DESeq2 and edgeR QL overlap, MA and dispersion plots, shrunken and unshrunken LFC, leading edge, sessionInfo

The ranking metric is stated in the output as the DESeq2 Wald statistic, with the reason for choosing it over the signed p-value and the shrunken fold change
Gene set size window 15-500 applied after intersection with the tested genes, and stated
Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways are run as separate passes with results reported separately and never pooled; the release/version of each collection is stated beside its results
The share of tested gene symbols that failed to map, and the share mapping many-to-many, is reported
Significant sets (BH-adjusted p < 0.05) are collapsed for redundancy, with one representative per group in the headline table and the full table as a supplement
Leading-edge genes with their Wald statistics are listed for each reported set, and overlap between leading edges is marked
The permutation seed is recorded
Every enrichment result carries the same confounding label as the gene-level results
If fewer than about 50 genes reach padj < 0.05, no over-representation test is run on that list; the ranked result stands alone and the size of the significant list is stated
If a requested collection is not present in the reference store, its absence is reported explicitly rather than substituted with another collection
constraints: Input is the full ranked list of every tested gene; do not cut the list at an adjusted p-value or a fold change before the test
Rank by the DESeq2 Wald statistic ('stat'), not by the unshrunken log2 fold change and not by a signed p-value
Universe is the set of genes tested in T1S2, never the whole genome or whole annotation
Use only human gene set collections — the data are Homo sapiens lung
Do not merge Hallmark, Reactome, and WikiPathways into one set list; a pathway present in two collections is one finding tested twice
Set min set size 15 and max set size 500 after intersecting each set with the tested genes
Set an explicit random seed and record it
Do not use KEGG (not served here) unless a licensed local copy with a stated release is supplied
caveats: Enrichment results are strongly method-dependent; a significant set is a hypothesis for follow-up, not a proven finding
Gene length and expression level bias count-based enrichment; using the tested genes as universe removes only the detection part of that bias
Because the gene-level statistics are confounded with batch, so is every pathway result derived from them — an enriched pathway may describe a processing difference
Gene symbols are unstable across annotation releases; the unmapped share must be reported rather than silently dropped

steps.name: Confounded-design report
steps.question: What can and cannot be concluded about treated versus control from these 12 lung samples, and with what numbers and diagnostics?
steps.description: Assemble the final report. Lead with the design limitation: batch B1 holds all 6 controls and batch B2 all 6 treated samples, so the reported effect is treatment + batch and the two are not identifiable; every number below inherits that caveat. Then state the method, the version of every package used, the design formula ~ condition, the contrast (condition, treated, control), the thresholds (padj < 0.05, BH, independent filtering on), the number of genes tested after filtering out of 12,000, and the number of differentially expressed genes. Include the two fit diagnostics — the MA plot with significant genes marked, and the dispersion plot with per-gene estimates, fitted trend, and shrunken values — placed before the gene tables, each with a sentence on what it shows. The gene table gives, per gene, the unshrunken log2 fold change, its standard error, and the apeglm-shrunken log2 fold change; rank genes and draw plots on the shrunken value, and keep the p-values from the unshrunken fit. Report the DESeq2 and edgeR quasi-likelihood significant-gene counts and their intersection, presenting the intersection as the high-confidence set and the method-unique genes as a secondary set named by method — do not present the union. Carry through the enrichment reporting from T2S1: collection and release, ranking metric, universe, size window, tool version, multiple-testing method, leading-edge genes per significant set, and the statement that enrichment results depend on the method. Close with the reproducibility record: sessionInfo, package versions, the permutation seed, and the version of each gene set collection. Finally, state what design would answer the question — treated and control samples distributed across both processing batches — and that re-running these same 12 samples with any correction method would not recover the answer.
steps.context: Consumes the DESeq2/edgeR results and diagnostics from T1S2 and the enrichment tables from T2S1.
acceptance_criteria: The confounding statement appears first in the report, not as a footnote, and names B1/control and B2/treated explicitly
Method, package versions, design formula, contrast, thresholds, number of genes tested, and number of DE genes are all stated before the gene tables
MA plot and dispersion plot are included, before the gene tables, each with a caption on what it shows
The gene table carries unshrunken log2FoldChange, lfcSE, and apeglm-shrunken log2FoldChange; ranking and plots use the shrunken value; p-values come from the unshrunken fit
DESeq2 and edgeR significant counts and the intersection size are reported; the intersection is labelled the high-confidence set and the union is not presented as the result
Enrichment reporting states database, release, ranking metric, universe, size window, tool version, and adjustment method, and lists leading-edge genes per significant set
A reproducibility record with sessionInfo, package versions, the seed, and collection versions is stored with the results
The report states explicitly that no gene on the list can be attributed to treatment rather than to processing batch, and names the design that would resolve it
constraints: Do not soften or omit the confounding caveat anywhere in the report
Rank genes by the shrunken log2 fold change; never by the unshrunken value alone
Do not present the union of DESeq2 and edgeR calls as the result
Store the reproducibility record with the results, not in a separate note
Make no causal or mechanistic claim about the treatment from these data
caveats: A reader given only a gene list from this design will over-interpret it; the report's job is to prevent that
Enrichment methods disagree on the same data — present sets as hypotheses

grounding.reason: Report contents follow the returned report-step claims: two-method overlap (R-0042), shrunken and unshrunken LFC (R-0085), MA and dispersion diagnostics (R-0087), method/version/design/threshold reporting (R-0041), enrichment provenance (R-0051), method-dependence caveat (R-0055), leading edge (R-0105), reproducibility record (R-0086).
